subject: Reproducibility and fluctuation of the INLA estimates

messages.author: e65db9bcd971d511
messages.subject: Reproducibility and fluctuation of the INLA estimates
parts:
Hi INLA users,

What I observed is that for the same data, if I run my model 2 times, there is a small variability. I wonder why this is the case (diff is the difference)? 
Is it due to the numerical integration is done in different ways or with some randomness? If so can we do something similar to set. seed(1)? 
The estimated hyperparameters also fluctuate a bit. I provide estimates of the fluctuation of one hyperparameter here based on 100 simulations.

Alokesh

PS: I am writing it as a separate question as some audience might be interested

messages.author: 9a89594e7fcb7aad
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Reproducibility and fluctuation of the INLA estimates
parts:
this is due to the parallel comptuations, which will make initial values for the
inner iteration. you can get replica using

inla(..., num.threads="1:1", control.compute=list(internal.opt=FALSE))

On Wed, 2025-05-07 at 10:33 +0300, Håvard Rue wrote:
> this is due to the parallel comptuations, which will make initial values for

> the .

this got cut short. the complete explantaion is
this is due to the parallel comptuations, which will make initial values for the

inner iteration depend on the results of the previous thread computations, which
we do not control, and this creates essentially the small variations. Of'corse,
this is also an iterative algorithm, hence there is a stopping rule in place, so
that will come in as well
